correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge5\) and every natural symmetry \(g\), an admissible vertex-orbit barycenter construction yields an exact PL homeomorphism of geometric fixed spaces with an independence complex on the orbit-conflict graph. Uniform enumeration of rotations and reflections yields the asserted circular, Möbius, open-ladder or empty conflict graphs, including all degenerate widths. An explicit two-step graph folding proves \(\operatorname{Ind}(L_k)\simeq S^{\lceil k/2\rceil-1}\) with \(k=1,2\) base cases. The published arXiv:2608.30601v2 full homotopy theorem supplies the remaining ambient types. A standalone exact checker found all 800 finite orbit isomorphisms for \(5\le n\le20\) and verified small homology; these checks support but do not replace the general proof.

evidence: Agarwal--Basak arXiv:2608.30601v2, Main Theorems 1--2, covers both *ambient* graph families but does not classify their subgroup fixed spaces.

originality.rationale: The primary paper treats ambient nonequivariant homotopy. The closest public symmetry theorem computes rational character and covers the layer-preserving reflection orbit-graph calculation, but neither the full mixed reflection/layer-exchange quotient classification nor the geometric homotopy types. The new complete fixed-locus theorem gives different sphere dimensions for reflections with identical Lefschetz data, so rational characters do not imply it. Established inputs and covered special cases are credited; equivalent unindexed work is a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed classification via graph quotients or independent equivariant simplicial methods could be equivalent.

Some parts, especially the layer-preserving reflection orbit identification, are direct published intermediary results; originality resides in the complete uniform fixed-point homotopy classification.
No independent human audit of the new theorem has occurred.

value.rationale: The recent homotopy classification and full rational automorphism representation naturally motivate determining actual fixed-locus topology. The new all-element theorem covers an infinite family and distinguishes mixed rotation/reflection/layer cases via exact sphere dimensions, rather than a small arbitrary parameter slice. Width twelve exhibits geometric \(S^3\) versus \(S^1\) fixed spaces with identical rational Lefschetz values. The general orbit-fixed-space lemma is standard and not asserted novel; value lies in the motivated complete graph-family classification.
